from.place: Proof paragraph 2, the displayed derived coefficient mapping-complex adjunction: evaluation at an identity extracts the universal map from a representing equivalence before applying the local coherent adjoint criterion.

title: Infinity Yoneda evaluation at the identity
statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$, and use quasicategories, mapping spaces and coherent transformations as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal E$ be a $\mathcal U'$-small quasicategory and have $\mathcal U$-small mapping spaces, let $\mathcal S$ denote the infinity category of $\mathcal U$-small spaces, and let $a\in\mathcal E$. Form the concrete rigidification functors of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces] for $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ first in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime}$, the infinity category of $\mathcal U\prime$-small spaces. Each admits a coherent $\mathcal S$-valued model: this means a functor into $\mathcal S$ equipped with a coherent natural equivalence, after the inclusion $\mathcal S\hookrightarrow\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime}$, to the corresponding concrete functor. Choose any such models; their distinguished identity points correspond under these equivalences to the singular identity vertices, up to the specified homotopies. Write $h_a(x)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,a)$ for the resulting coherent representable presheaf; mapping-space notation here denotes its value up to the comparison equivalence, rather than equality of underlying simplicial sets. For every coherent presheaf $P:\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$, evaluation at $\operatorname{id}_a$ induces an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)}(h_a,P)\simeq P(a),\qquad \alpha\longmapsto\alpha_a(\operatorname{id}_a).$$
Its inverse sends $p\in P(a)$ to the coherent transformation whose component at $x$ is $f\mapsto P(f)(p)$ for $f:x\to a$. Thus for any coherent transformation $\alpha:h_a\to P$, its component maps are homotopic to $f\mapsto P(f)(\alpha_a(\operatorname{id}_a))$, coherently in $x$ and in parameters in the mapping spaces. Dually, for $Q:\mathcal E\to\mathcal S$ and $h^a(x)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(a,x)$, evaluation gives $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E,\mathcal S)}(h^a,Q)\simeq Q(a)$ with inverse $q\mapsto(f\mapsto Q(f)(q))$. These are equivalences of full spaces of coherent transformations, not just bijections on homotopy classes.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 8.3.1.3 (03M5), with evaluation defined in Notation 8.3.1.2 (03M4); apply also to the opposite category. Definition 5.6.6.1 (038A) gives the action on a universal element, and Theorem 5.6.6.13 (038J) supplies the coherent representable functor. Read online; not archived in literature/. These are Kerodon identifiers; no corresponding Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical assertion.

proof.text:
Work first covariantly in $C$, with $a\in C$, and take the actual rigidification functor $H$ of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Put $A=\mathfrak C[C]$, $M_x=\operatorname{Map}^{R}_C(a,x)$, and let $\eta\in H(a)$ be the singular identity vertex. Let $\lambda_x$ be the identity-action cocone and $e_x:M_x\to H(x)$ its point map, exactly as specified in [lem-coef-rigidification-identity-action]. That lemma identifies the actual map by the equation
$$[e_x][p_{M_x}]=[u_{a,x}][\theta_{C,a,x}].$$
Both $p_{M_x}$ and $\theta_{C,a,x}$ are weak homotopy equivalences by [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution]; $u_{a,x}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for the arbitrary simplicial set $A(a,x)$ by [lem-cbc-realization-singular-unit-weak]. Hence $[e_x]$ is invertible. The weak-equivalence clause of [lem-coef-rigidification-identity-action] asserts this conclusion for the actual simplicial point map $e_x$. As spaces are considered up to weak homotopy equivalence, it is an equivalence of full spaces. This proves that $\eta$ is a universal identity element for the defined functor. It is a theorem proved here, not an additional hypothesis or a change of the definition. Take the value universe here to be $\mathcal U\prime$, so the concrete $H$ is defined: its rigidification is a colimit over a $\mathcal U\prime$-small simplex category and all its mapping simplicial sets and singular realizations are $\mathcal U\prime$-small. Local smallness does not imply that these concrete values are $\mathcal U$-small. Steps 6--8 will construct coherent smaller models using the proved equivalences $e_x$ and $\mathcal U$-small Kan complexes weakly equivalent to $M_x$.

source.place: Section 2.2.4 opening paragraph and Proposition 2.2.4.1; Section 5.1.3 construction. Identity-action formula and two-out-of-three expanded explicitly.

proof.text: For $x\in C$, [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] identifies the strict fiber $\{a\}\times_C C_{/x}$ with $M_x$. Its universal-arrow family is the right-pinch prism of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. Thus the local cocone induced by the point $\eta:*\to H(a)$ is exactly $\lambda_x$ of [lem-coef-rigidification-identity-action], not an arbitrarily chosen cocone with apex $H(x)$. Step 1 proves that its point map $e_x$ is a weak equivalence. By [lem-coef-space-point-cocone-criterion], this actual cocone is colimiting. Apply that criterion with $\mathcal W=\mathcal U\prime$. Here $M_x\subseteq C_{n+1}$ degreewise is $\mathcal U\prime$-small because $C$ is, while $H(x)$ is $\mathcal U\prime$-small by Step 1; no $\mathcal U$-smallness of $M_x$ is used in this step. No colimit indexed by the whole ambient category is used.

source.place: Lemma 8.3.1.7, proof: actual identity-action cocone on the mapping-space index; with Example 7.1.2.10.

proof.text:
Take $K=\Delta^0$, $\delta:K\to C$ the vertex $a$, $F_0=*$, $F=H$, and $\beta=\eta$ in [lem-coef-pointwise-lan-mapping-property]. Its local indexing object at $x$ is exactly $M_x$, and its local cocone is the one proved colimiting in Step 2. For every $Q:C\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime}$, the conclusion gives an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(C,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime})}(H,Q)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime}}(*,Q(a)),\qquad\alpha\longmapsto\alpha_a\eta.$$
The case $K=\Delta^0$ of [lem-coef-space-point-cocone-criterion] identifies the target with $Q(a)$ by its family-of-points map. The resulting equivalence is consequently the specified evaluation $\Phi(\alpha)=\alpha_a(\operatorname{id}_a)$. All functor categories are formed in a universe containing $\mathcal U'$, as permitted by the cited theorem; this establishes evaluation first for the concrete larger-valued functor, before the descent in Steps 6--10.

source.place: Proposition 8.3.1.3, proof via Lemma 8.3.1.7 and Proposition 7.3.6.1; Notation 8.3.1.2 specifies evaluation.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-infinity-parameterized-evaluation-naturality] with $F=H$, $G=Q$ and the singular identity point $\eta$. The point map of its cocone is exactly the $e_x$ specified in [lem-coef-rigidification-identity-action]. Thus on the full product of the transformation space and $M_x$ there is a homotopy
$$\alpha_xe_x\simeq\bigl(f\longmapsto Q(f)(\alpha_a(\eta))\bigr),$$
with the parameter and $x$-coherences asserted by the new lemma. Step 1 proves $e_x$ is an equivalence and identifies its identity point. No right-pinched composition on the different complex $H(x)$ is substituted for this map.

source.place: Definition 5.6.6.1 specifies action on an element; parameterized naturality gives the inverse formula once Step 3 proves evaluation is an equivalence.

proof.text: Let $\Phi$ be the full-space evaluation equivalence of Step 3. Its source and target are Kan complexes (the mapping space by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]); [lem-cbc-kan-whitehead-inverse] supplies a map $s$ with homotopies $\Phi s\simeq1$ and $s\Phi\simeq1$. Substitute the whole family $s:Q(a)\to T$ into Step 4, rather than choosing a separate transformation for each vertex. Using $\Phi s\simeq1$ gives $(s(q))_xe_x\simeq(f\mapsto Q(f)(q))$. Since $e_x$ is an equivalence, this is the required inverse formula through the stated mapping-space comparison. Substituting $\Phi(\alpha)$ and using $s\Phi\simeq1$ gives reconstruction of every $\alpha$, with the same full parameter homotopies. This proves the larger-valued covariant clause.

source.place: Definition 5.6.6.1 specifies action on an element; parameterized naturality gives the inverse formula once Step 3 proves evaluation is an equivalence.

proof.text: Let $\iota:\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime}$ be inclusion. The coherent-nerve construction of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces] makes it the full simplicial subset on the smaller Kan complexes: an enriched simplex with these vertices has the same function simplicial sets and subset-chain data in either universe. In particular every right-pinched mapping simplex between smaller vertices is the same in both nerves, so $\iota$ is fully faithful. This uses the definition of a full subcategory and the degreewise right-pinched convention in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Theorem 4.8.4.1 on the full essential image; the universe inclusion is checked directly on enriched simplices. Agent-written size descent following the concrete comparison, preserving the original small value universe.

proof.text:
Produce a $\mathcal U$-small Kan complex $Y_x$ and a weak equivalence $k_x:Y_x\to M_x$. For $C=\mathcal E$ this is exactly local smallness; if a chosen comparison points the other way, use [lem-cbc-kan-whitehead-inverse] to reverse it. For $C=\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$, choose $Y'\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,a)$ by the same hypothesis and put $Y_x=Y'^{\mathrm{op}}$. The interval-reversal and barycentric-reversal calculation retained in Step 11 identifies the opposite arrow space with $U_{\mathcal E}(x,a)^{\mathrm{op}}$ and preserves weak equivalences. Order reversal takes $\Lambda_i^n$ to $\Lambda_{n-i}^n$, so $Y_x$ is still Kan and small. The natural homotopy equivalences $j$ of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] give
$$Y'^{\mathrm{op}}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,a)^{\mathrm{op}}\xrightarrow{j^{\mathrm{op}}}U_{\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}}(a,x)\xrightarrow{j^{-1}}M_x.$$
This composite is $k_x$. Opposites preserve homotopies because $(\Delta^1)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\Delta^1$. All compositions here are actual simplicial maps; no claim that the large concrete value $H(x)$ is itself small is made.

source.place: Theorem 4.8.4.1 on the full essential image; the universe inclusion is checked directly on enriched simplices. Agent-written size descent following the concrete comparison, preserving the original small value universe.

proof.text: For either variance set $g_x=e_xk_x:Y_x\to H(x)$. It is a weak equivalence between Kan complexes by Step 1, Step 7 and [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. The new [lem-coef-kan-weak-equivalence-space-edge] turns this actual map into an equivalence edge of $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime}$, with both inverse triangles. Thus $H$ lands in the full replete essential image $\mathcal T$ of $\iota$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image] to the fully faithful inclusion proved in Step 6, in auxiliary universes containing these categories. Its quasi-inverse $L:\mathcal T\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ gives the coherent small model $h^a=LH$ and a coherent equivalence $v:\iota h^a\simeq H$. This constructs a coherent model, including its higher data, rather than independently picking its values. Apply an inverse of $v_a$ to $\eta$ to obtain $\eta_0\in h^a(a)$ with $v_a(\eta_0)\simeq\eta$.

source.place: Theorem 4.8.4.1 on the full essential image; the universe inclusion is checked directly on enriched simplices. Agent-written size descent following the concrete comparison, preserving the original small value universe.

proof.text: For two smaller-valued diagrams $A,B:C\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$, the full right-pinched transformation spaces before and after $\iota$ are identical. Indeed their $n$-simplices are maps $C\times\Delta^{n+1}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime}$ whose restriction to the initial face is $A$ and whose last vertex is $B$. Every vertex of such a map is a value of $A$ or $B$, hence lies in the smaller full subcategory of Step 6. Therefore the entire map factors uniquely through $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$. Restrictions give identical simplicial operators. This follows directly from the internal-functor and full-subcategory definitions in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Theorem 4.8.4.1 on the full essential image; the universe inclusion is checked directly on enriched simplices. Agent-written size descent following the concrete comparison, preserving the original small value universe.

proof.text: Let $w$ be an inverse of $v$ in the functor quasicategory. Composition as in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] gives mutually inverse maps up to homotopy between $\operatorname{Map}(H,\iota Q)$ and $\operatorname{Map}(\iota h^a,\iota Q)$ for every small-valued $Q$: associativity identifies their composites with composition by $vw$ and $wv$, and the inverse triangles and unit laws identify these with the identities. Use Step 9 to identify the latter space with $\operatorname{Map}(h^a,Q)$ in the smaller universe. Evaluation commutes with composition; the equation $v_a(\eta_0)\simeq\eta$ therefore identifies the Step 3 equivalence with evaluation at $\eta_0$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-parameterized-evaluation-naturality] to $F=\iota h^a$, $G=H$, the point $\eta_0$ and transformation $v$: it identifies $v_xe^{h^a}_{\eta_0,x}$ with $e^H_{\eta,x}$ on the full arrow family. The inverse and reconstruction homotopies of Step 5 consequently give exactly $f\mapsto Q(f)(q)$ for the small model, with all parameters. Any other stipulated small model has its own equivalence $v$ to $H$ and corresponding identity point, so the identical argument applies to it. No uniqueness of a choice is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 4.8.4.1 on the full essential image; the universe inclusion is checked directly on enriched simplices. Agent-written size descent following the concrete comparison, preserving the original small value universe.

proof.text:
For the contravariant clause apply Steps 1--10 to $C=\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$, $Q=P$, and the object $a$. Opposite mapping-space conventions agree as spaces as follows. Put $U_D(x,y)=\{x\}\times_D\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D)\times_D\{y\}$. Reversal of the interval gives $U_{\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}}(a,x)=U_{\mathcal E}(x,a)^{\mathrm{op}}$. By [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] both right-pinched models map into these arrow spaces by natural homotopy equivalences. For a Kan complex $T$, reversal of barycentric coordinates gives a natural homeomorphism $|T^{\mathrm{op}}|\cong|T|$: it sends $[t,(r_0,\ldots,r_n)]$ to $[t,(r_n,\ldots,r_0)]$. The realization identifications of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] make this well-defined, and it is its own inverse. It follows that $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}}(a,x)$ models $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,a)$ as a space. The coherent representable is the one on the opposite category, before taking this pointwise comparison; reversing the composition diagrams turns its postcomposition action into precomposition. In particular its distinguished point is still $\operatorname{id}_a$. Therefore the small-model evaluation equivalence of Steps 6--10 becomes
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)}(h_a,P)\simeq P(a).$$
The coherent small model on the opposite category is defined by Steps 6--10, with its identity point corresponding to the singular identity. The arrow $a\to x$ in $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ is $f:x\to a$ in $\mathcal E$, so the Step 5 inverse reads $p\mapsto(f\mapsto P(f)(p))$, with the same two inverse homotopies and simplicial parameter coherence. Only equivalences of models are used, not a strict identification of left- and right-pinched simplicial sets.

source.place: Remark 8.3.3.6, opposite duality; explicit interval and barycentric reversal checks retained.
